title: Utility difficulty and energy assistance sit beside following-month food insecurity and severity
source_unit: identified SIPP person-month pairs; utility or energy-assistance status at month t and food-security status at month t+1

observations.period: 2024 reference year; utility-payment difficulty at month t and food security at month t+1

denominator.unit: eligible person-month pairs; valid food-security pair n=24,297

following_food_insecurity.unit: person-weighted percent; Fay-BRR SE 2.2694 pp; approximate 95% CI 46.6806–55.5768

observations.method: Same-person adjacent-month descriptive screen using valid EAWBGAS/AAWBGAS at month t, RFOODS/AFOODS at month t+1, November-to-December and all consecutive month pairs, WPFINWGT at month t, and 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights.
observations.uncertainty: Utility and food fields may be reference-period or household measures repeated on person-month rows; this is not a household prevalence or dated bill estimate.
observations.subgroup: Person-month pairs reporting utility-payment difficulty at month t.
observations.counterinterpretation: The difference may reflect persistent household need, season, health, income, household composition, geography, or field selection rather than a utility condition causing food insecurity.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; no utility-payment difficulty at month t and food security at month t+1

denominator.unit: eligible person-month pairs; valid food-security pair n=321,986

following_food_insecurity.unit: person-weighted percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.3298 pp; approximate 95% CI 7.7570–9.0497

observations.method: Same-person adjacent-month descriptive comparison using the same SIPP fields, validity rules, weights, and Fay-BRR procedure as the utility-difficulty observation.
observations.uncertainty: The no-difficulty comparison does not control for income, season, health, household composition, or selection into the utility field.
observations.subgroup: Person-month pairs reporting no utility-payment difficulty at month t.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower following food-insecurity share does not establish that utility stability protected food security; the groups may differ before the screen.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; energy assistance at month t and food security at month t+1

denominator.unit: eligible person-month pairs; valid food-security pair n=13,399

following_food_insecurity.unit: person-weighted percent; Fay-BRR SE 2.9023 pp; approximate 95% CI 27.0740–38.4512

observations.method: Same-person adjacent-month descriptive screen using valid EENERGY_ASST at month t, RFOODS/AFOODS at month t+1, WPFINWGT, and 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights.
observations.uncertainty: Energy assistance is targeted and conditional; the estimate cannot distinguish program support from pre-existing need or selection.
observations.subgroup: Person-month pairs reporting energy assistance at month t.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher food insecurity among assistance recipients may reflect the need that prompted assistance, incomplete adequacy, seasonal composition, or reporting selection rather than an adverse assistance effect.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; no energy assistance at month t and food security at month t+1

denominator.unit: eligible person-month pairs; valid food-security pair n=178,141

following_food_insecurity.unit: person-weighted percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.6088 pp; approximate 95% CI 15.7410–18.1277

observations.method: Same-person adjacent-month descriptive comparison using valid EENERGY_ASST code 2, RFOODS/AFOODS, WPFINWGT, and 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights.
observations.uncertainty: The comparison is conditional on an assistance field and does not control for eligibility, need, geography, season, health, or household composition.
observations.subgroup: Person-month pairs reporting no energy assistance at month t.
observations.counterinterpretation: The lower comparison share cannot be interpreted as an assistance effect or a counterfactual food-security rate.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; utility-payment difficulty and energy assistance at month t; food security at month t+1

denominator.unit: eligible person-month pairs; valid food-security pair n=3,772

following_food_insecurity.unit: person-weighted percent; Fay-BRR SE 5.6640 pp; approximate 95% CI 50.6237–72.8266

following_food_security_severity.value: high or marginal 38.27%; low 24.83%; very low 36.89%
following_food_security_severity.unit: person-weighted category distribution; Fay-BRR SEs 5.66, 4.61, and 5.70 percentage points respectively

observations.method: Same-person adjacent-month joint descriptive screen using valid utility and energy-assistance fields at month t, RFOODS/AFOODS at month t+1, WPFINWGT, and 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights.
observations.uncertainty: The joint cell is conditional and targeted; its higher following food insecurity is not an assistance effect.
observations.subgroup: Person-month pairs reporting utility-payment difficulty and energy assistance at month t.
observations.counterinterpretation: Assistance may be reaching households with greater underlying need or incomplete protection; persistent need, season, health, and composition remain alternatives.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; utility-payment difficulty and no energy assistance at month t; food security at month t+1

denominator.unit: eligible person-month pairs; valid food-security pair n=16,879

following_food_insecurity.unit: person-weighted percent; Fay-BRR SE 2.7888 pp; approximate 95% CI 48.3446–59.2767

observations.method: Same-person adjacent-month joint descriptive comparison using the same SIPP fields, validity rules, weights, and Fay-BRR procedure as the assisted difficulty observation.
observations.uncertainty: The no-assistance cell is not a counterfactual; it differs in eligibility, need, and other composition.
observations.subgroup: Person-month pairs reporting utility-payment difficulty and no energy assistance at month t.
observations.counterinterpretation: The lower share may reflect less underlying need or different field selection rather than a protective effect of nonreceipt.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; no utility-payment difficulty and energy assistance at month t; food security at month t+1

denominator.unit: eligible person-month pairs; valid food-security pair n=9,627

following_food_insecurity.unit: person-weighted percent; Fay-BRR SE 2.7069 pp; approximate 95% CI 15.6818–26.2928

observations.method: Same-person adjacent-month joint descriptive comparison using valid utility and energy-assistance fields at month t, RFOODS/AFOODS at month t+1, WPFINWGT, and 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights.
observations.uncertainty: The cell is conditional and does not identify why assistance was received despite no reported utility-payment difficulty.
observations.subgroup: Person-month pairs reporting no utility-payment difficulty and energy assistance at month t.
observations.counterinterpretation: The assistance status may reflect another energy or household need not captured by the utility-difficulty screen.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; no utility-payment difficulty and no energy assistance at month t; food security at month t+1

denominator.unit: eligible person-month pairs; valid food-security pair n=161,262

following_food_insecurity.unit: person-weighted percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.5443 pp; approximate 95% CI 12.0115–14.1450

observations.method: Same-person adjacent-month joint descriptive comparison using valid utility and energy-assistance fields at month t, RFOODS/AFOODS at month t+1, WPFINWGT, and 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights.
observations.uncertainty: The comparison is conditional and is not a counterfactual food-security rate.
observations.subgroup: Person-month pairs reporting no utility-payment difficulty and no energy assistance at month t.
observations.counterinterpretation: The lower share may reflect lower baseline need or composition rather than a benefit of nonreceipt.

related_sources.claim: Official SIPP definitions, codes, universes, and status flags.
Official 240-replicate-weight archive used for Fay-BRR variance.

reproduction_audit.result: The full-file rerun reproduced the four marginal and four joint output cells and added high-or-marginal, low, and very-low food-security distributions; raw inputs remain outside the repository.

boundary: This is an adjacent-month descriptive SIPP transition screen. Utility and energy-assistance fields may be reference-period or conditional household measures repeated on person-month rows, and food security is not necessarily newly measured at month t+1. No dated bill shock, assistance effect, food recovery, work/care substitution, trust, political action, or household prevalence claim is made.
